sentences.text: Easwaran S., J.
The present appeal is preferred by the claimants aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 31.1.2017 in L.A.R. No.757 of 2015 on the files of the Principal Sub Court, Kozhikode.
2. The facts in brief for disposal of the appeal are as follows:

An extent of 0.0189 hectares of land comprised in Re-survey No.261/5 of Chevayur Amsom Desom of Kozhikode Taluk was acquired by the Government for the purpose K Sobha vs District Collector, Kozhikode on 2 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21782917/
2 of widening the Panath Thazham - CWRDM Road.

sentences.text: Section 4(1) notification was issued on 25.8.2011 and possession was taken on 8.11.2013.
The Land Acquisition Officer, fixed the land value at Rs.5,62,988/- as total compensation.

Aggrieved by the award, the claimants approached the Reference Court by filing L.A.R. No.757 of 2015 under Section 18 of the erst while Land LA.APP. NO. 406 OF 2017 4 2024:KER:81450 Acquisition Act, 1894.
On behalf of the claimants, Exts.A1 and A2 documents were produced.
The 4th claimant was examined as AW1.
An Advocate Commissioner was appointed for local inspection of the property and Ext.X1 was marked as the commission report and Ext.X2 was marked as the sketch.
On behalf of the respondents Award No.141 of 2013 dated 7.11.2013 was produced.
The Reference Court, by impugned judgment and decree, enhanced the compensation by Rs.5 Lakhs per cent from the date of notification i,e., 25.8.2011.

3. We have heard Sri. Arun Krishna Dhan , the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellants and Sri. T.K. Shajahan, the learned Senior Government Pleader appearing on behalf of the respondents.
4. Sri. Arun Krishna Dhan, the learned counsel appearing for the appellants contended that the land acquired were located in the prime area of the Kozhikode Corporation.
Ext.A2, being the assignment deed executed in the year 2010, was not properly considered by the Reference Court.

As per Ext.A2,
the property was purchased for an amount of Rs.12 Lakhs.

However, the Advocate Commissioner,
after LA.APP. NO. 406 OF 2017 5 2024:KER:81450 visiting the property and conducting local inspection, opined that the property would fetch nearly Rs.10 Lakhs.
It is contended that the reliance placed by the Reference Court in Ext.A1 for enhancing the compensation was without any basis.
He further pointed out that by relying on Ext.A1, the Reference Court had totally misconstrued the purpose for which Ext.A1 was produced.
He further added that Ext.A1 was in respect of property which was nearly six kilometers away from the present acquired land.
Both these properties were acquired for the same purpose and amount of Rs.4.5 Lakhs per cent was granted for the properties lying Six (6) Kilometers away from the acquired land.
With reference to Ext.X2 sketch, the learned counsel contended that the acquired land is close to the Wayanad road and also nearby to the Medical College.
The commercial importance of the locality also stood proved beyond doubt as per Ext.X1 report of the Advocate Commissioner and Ext.X2 sketch.
Therefore, the Reference Court was not justified in fixing the land value at Rs.5 Lakhs per cent.
5. On the other hand, the learned Senior Government Pleader appearing on behalf of the respondents reiterated the findings in the LA.APP. NO. 406 OF 2017 6 2024:KER:81450 judgment under appeal.
He pointed out that Ext.A2 could not have been relied on by the Reference Court since Ext.A2 is dated 21.1.2010.
The price quoted for the land under Ext.A2 is highly excessive and that cannot form the basis for determination of the compensation in respect of the acquired land.

He further pointed out that under Ext.A1, in respect of the same acquisition, Rs.4.5 Lakhs alone was granted by the Reference Court as enhanced compensation and, therefore, on a reasonable assumption, the Reference Court has fixed the land value at Rs.5 Lakhs does not call for any interference by this Court and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

sentences.text: We have considered the rival submissions raised across the Bar.
7. The commercial importance of the land acquired cannot be disputed.
The acquired land is a part of Chevarambalam town and the Kozhikode Medical College is just two Kilometers away from it.
Several commercially important buildings are situated in the close vicinity of the acquired land.
RP mall, Civil Station, Eranhipalam temple, church, mosque, schools, colleges and other industrial and business LA.APP
KER:81450 establishments are situated within the range of three kilometers from the acquired land.
A perusal of Ext.X2 sketch shows the vast difference between the basic land on which the Land Acquisition Officer has calculated the compensation.

The Advocate Commissioner has reported the existence of commercially important buildings which fortifies the case of the appellants that the acquired land is situated in a more commercially important area.
8.
It is pertinent to mention that under Ext.A1, the Reference Court had fixed the amount of Rs.4.5 Lakhs towards the land value per cent.
The specific case of the appellants is that the said land is more than six kilometers away from the acquired land has not even being adverted to by the Reference Court.
It may be true that the acquired land and the land under Ext.A2 are not similar in nature.
Perhaps, it could be said that the land under Ext.A2 is abutting the National Highway.
But that by itself will not erode the commercial importance of the acquired land.
It is pertinent to mention that the Reference Court had taken note of the importance of the acquired land as reported by the Advocate Commissioner.
If that be so, the LA.APP. NO. 406 OF 2017 8 2024:KER:81450 Reference Court ought to have been given specific reasons as to why it fixed the land value at Rs.5 Lakhs.
9. A perusal of the judgment of the Reference Court shows that the amount of Rs.5 Lakhs was fixed on a guess work.

Though the fixation of the land value in land acquisition cases on guess work is permissible under law, we cannot subscribe to the findings of the trial court as to why it has not accepted Ext.X1 report of the Advocate Commissioner and Ext.X2 sketch which proves the commercial importance of the acquired land.
Pertinently, the Advocate Commissioner, after conducting local inspection has reported that the land will fetch Rs.10 Lakhs per cent.
It is to be noted that the report of the Advocate Commissioner remains unchallenged.

Except, Ext.R1 award,
no other document has been produced by the respondent/State.

Therefore, in the light of these overwhelming facts, especially when the report of the Advocate Commissioner remains unchallenged, we are of the considered view that the Reference Court was not justified in fixing the land value of the acquired land at Rs.5 Lakhs per cent.
As a result of the above discussion, we are of the considered view that the appellant is entitled to succeed.
Resultantly, the appeal is allowed.
The judgment and decree in L.A.R. No.757 of 2015 dated 31.1.2017 is modified and the land value of the acquired land is fixed at Rs.10 Lakhs per cent.
The appellant is entitled to get all statutory benefits flowing out of the respective land value.
The appellant is also entitled to get proportionate cost.
